classes.symptoms: Water-soaked angular leaf spots, leaf blighting, wilting of young shoots, and gum exudation on stems and petioles.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply copper oxychloride (2.5g/L) or Bordeaux mixture. Prune and burn infected shoots immediately. Use neem-based botanical formulations.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Streptocycline (100-200 ppm) mixed with Copper Oxychloride (0.2%).
classes.prevention: Use certified disease-free stem cuttings, rotate crops with non-hosts (maize or legumes), and disinfect pruning tools with 70% alcohol.
classes.weather_action_rule: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation when humidity exceeds 85% to prevent bacterial splash dispersion.

classes.symptoms: Small brown circular to angular spots with dark distinct margins on mature lower leaves, causing premature defoliation.
classes.organic_treatment: Spray wettable sulfur (2g/L) or potassium bicarbonate. Ensure plant spacing for sunlight penetration.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar application of Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5g/L) or Carbendazim 50% WP (1g/L).
classes.prevention: Ensure wide inter-row spacing (1m x 1m), remove and destroy lower diseased leaves, and maintain balanced potassium fertilization.
classes.weather_action_rule: Delay fungicide spraying if heavy rain (>15mm) is forecasted within the next 4 hours.

classes.symptoms: Vibrant green palmate foliage without spots, chlorosis, curling, or stem lesions.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply balanced organic compost and vermicompost every 45 days.
classes.chemical_treatment: No chemical intervention needed. Maintain standard NPK (10:10:20) schedule.
classes.prevention: Regular field scouting, weed control, and preventive biocontrol sprays of Trichoderma viride.
classes.weather_action_rule: Maintain standard irrigation intervals based on soil tensiometer readings.

classes.symptoms: Severe chlorotic mosaic pattern on leaves, leaf distortion, stunted growth, and reduced root tuber yield.
classes.pathogen: Cassava mosaic virus (CMV) transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)
classes.organic_treatment: Spray yellow sticky traps (15 traps/acre) to control whitefly vector. Spray 5% neem seed kernel extract (NSKE).
classes.chemical_treatment: Control whitefly vector with Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (0.5ml/L) or Thiamethoxam 25% WG (0.3g/L).
classes.prevention: Rogue and burn infected plants immediately. Plant certified CMV-resistant cultivars (e.g., TME 419).
classes.weather_action_rule: Hot dry weather (>32°C) accelerates whitefly reproduction; increase vector scouting frequency.

classes.symptoms: Soft, discolored, foul-smelling rotting tubers, yellowing foliage, sudden wilting, and collapse of above-ground plant.
classes.pathogen: Phytophthora spp., Fusarium oxysporum, Pythium spp. (Fungal/Oomycete)
classes.organic_treatment: Drench root zone with Trichoderma harzianum bio-fungicide (10g/L). Improve soil drainage with ridge planting.
classes.chemical_treatment: Soil drenching with Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (2.5g/L) or Ridomil Gold.
classes.prevention: Avoid waterlogging; plant on raised ridges or mounds (30-40cm). Practice 3-year crop rotation.
classes.weather_action_rule: Halt irrigation immediately if soil moisture exceeds 80% and rain is expected.

classes.symptoms: Small, yellowish-to-brown spots on leaf blades, sheaths, and stalks, often coalescing into chocolate brown bands.
classes.organic_treatment: Bio-agent application of Bacillus subtilis and foliar compost tea.
classes.chemical_treatment: Spray Azoxystrobin (18.2%) + Difenoconazole (11.4%) SC at 1ml/L or Pyraclostrobin.
classes.prevention: Deep tillage to bury crop residue, use tolerant corn hybrids, and ensure adequate crop nutrition.
classes.weather_action_rule: Favorable during warm, humid conditions with free water in the whorl.

classes.symptoms: Internal decay of the lower stalk with shredded appearance and numerous tiny black microsclerotia resembling charcoal dust.
classes.organic_treatment: Soil enrichment with farmyard manure and Trichoderma bio-formulations.
classes.chemical_treatment: Seed treatment with Thiram 75% WP (3g/kg seed) or Carbendazim (2g/kg seed).
classes.prevention: Maintain adequate soil moisture during post-flowering to relieve plant drought stress.
classes.weather_action_rule: High risk during extended hot (>35°C), drought-stressed periods; schedule emergency light irrigation.

classes.symptoms: Pale yellow, elongated chlorotic streaks or spots running parallel to the leaf veins.
classes.pathogen: Viral / Physiological chlorosis or early fungal infection
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar application of micronutrient mixture (Zinc, Iron, Magnesium) plus sea-weed extract.
classes.chemical_treatment: Zinc sulphate (0.5%) + Ferrous sulphate (0.2%) foliar spray.
classes.prevention: Soil testing to rectify micronutrient deficiencies; control aphid and leafhopper vectors.
classes.weather_action_rule: Monitor soil pH; alkaline soils (pH > 7.8) induce micronutrient lockup.

classes.symptoms: Distinct rectangular, tan-to-gray lesions restricted between leaf veins with sharp parallel edges.
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar spray of Potassium silicate and bio-fungicides (Trichoderma).
classes.chemical_treatment: Spray Pyraclostrobin + Fluxapyroxad or Azoxystrobin 23% SC (1ml/L).
classes.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids, practice residue management (minimum 2-year non-host rotation).
classes.weather_action_rule: Thrives in overcast conditions with >90% RH for over 12 hours.

classes.symptoms: Broad, deep green leaves with strong erect stalks and healthy cob formation without discoloration.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply balanced vermicompost and Azotobacter / PSB bio-fertilizers.
classes.chemical_treatment: Follow recommended NPK dosage (120:60:40 kg/ha) in split applications.
classes.prevention: Routine weeding, insect scouting for fall armyworm, and proper water management.
classes.weather_action_rule: Maintain optimal irrigation schedule based on tasseling and grain-filling stages.

classes.symptoms: Shot-holes in whorl leaves, ragged leaf margins, sawdust-like frass inside whorls (Fall Armyworm / Stem Borer).
classes.organic_treatment: Release Trichogramma pretiosum parasitoids (50,000/acre). Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) @ 2g/L or Neem oil (1500 ppm).
classes.chemical_treatment: Whorl application of Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (0.4ml/L) or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG (0.4g/L).
classes.prevention: Install pheromone traps (5 traps/acre), intercrop with desmodium/push-pull strategy.
classes.weather_action_rule: Scout actively during warm evenings when adult moth flight activity peaks.

classes.symptoms: Pale yellow chlorotic striping on leaves with downy white fungal growth on the lower surface in morning dew.
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar spray with Copper Hydroxide (2g/L) and remove systemic infected plants.
classes.chemical_treatment: Seed treatment with Metalaxyl-M (Apron XL) @ 2ml/kg, foliar spray of Metalaxyl-Mancozeb @ 2.5g/L.
classes.prevention: Use resistant maize hybrids and avoid sowing near sorghum fields.
classes.weather_action_rule: Dew-laden cool nights (18-22°C) followed by humid mornings trigger sporulation.

classes.symptoms: Intense reddish-purple coloration on leaf tips, margins, and lower stalks, especially in young seedlings.
classes.pathogen: Phosphorus deficiency induced by cold soil or root damage
classes.organic_treatment: Apply rock phosphate with Phosphate Solubilizing Bacteria (PSB). Soil warming with shallow hoeing.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray of 19:19:19 (N:P:K) or DAP (2%) solution.
classes.prevention: Incorporate starter phosphorus fertilizer near seed row during sowing.
classes.weather_action_rule: Cold soils (<15°C) restrict root phosphorus uptake; symptoms usually subside as temperatures rise.

classes.symptoms: Large, fleshy, white-to-silvery galls on tassels, ears, stalks, and leaves that rupture to release black powdery spores.
classes.organic_treatment: Remove and incinerate galls before the outer membrane breaks and releases black chlamydospores.
classes.chemical_treatment: Seed dressing with Carboxin 37.5% + Thiram 37.5% DS (2g/kg seed).
classes.prevention: Avoid mechanical damage to stalks and roots during cultivation. Maintain balanced nitrogen.
classes.weather_action_rule: Wounds created by hailstorms or insect damage provide entry points.

classes.symptoms: Narrow, discontinuous chlorotic streaks along leaf veins, starting as minute translucent spots on young leaves.
classes.pathogen: Maize streak virus (MSV) transmitted by leafhoppers (Cicadulina spp.)
classes.organic_treatment: Spray botanical insect repellent (Neem 1500 ppm @ 3ml/L) to suppress leafhopper vector.
classes.chemical_treatment: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70% WS (5g/kg seed). Foliar spray of Thiamethoxam 25% WG (0.3g/L).
classes.prevention: Plant MSV-resistant hybrids; avoid planting downwind from older infected cereal crops.
classes.weather_action_rule: High leafhopper migrations occur after prolonged dry spells followed by rain.

classes.symptoms: Broad chlorotic stripes along veins, apical bending, stunting, and failure of tassel emergence.
classes.pathogen: Maize stripe virus (MSpV) transmitted by corn planthopper (Peregrinus maidis)
classes.organic_treatment: Application of entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana @ 5g/L.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray of Dinotefuran 20% SG (0.5g/L) or Pymetrozine 50% WG.
classes.prevention: Synchronized regional planting and systematic eradication of grassy weed hosts.
classes.weather_action_rule: Plan irrigation to avoid excessive humidity favoring planthopper swarms.

classes.symptoms: Abnormal deep violet-to-bronze pigmentation on foliage, often combined with stunted root growth.
classes.pathogen: Severe abiotic stress / Aluminum toxicity / Extreme phosphorus immobilization in acidic soils
classes.organic_treatment: Apply agricultural lime or dolomite (1-2 tons/ha) to adjust acidic soil pH.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar application of mono-potassium phosphate (00:52:34) @ 5g/L.
classes.prevention: Conduct soil pH testing; maintain soil pH between 6.0 and 7.0 with regular liming.
classes.weather_action_rule: High water table exacerbates root anaerobic stress in acidic soils.

classes.symptoms: Circular to oval bright yellow spots on leaf blades with yellow halos.
classes.pathogen: Curvularia lunata / Early stage foliar fungal spotting
classes.organic_treatment: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens bio-formulation (10g/L).
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray of Propiconazole 25% EC (1ml/L) or Chlorothalonil 75% WP (2g/L).
classes.prevention: Balanced potassium fertilization and clean cultivation.
classes.weather_action_rule: Spray when wind speed is <10 km/h to minimize drift.

classes.symptoms: V-shaped yellowing starting from leaf tips moving down the midrib of older leaves (Nitrogen Deficiency).
classes.pathogen: Nutritional deficiency (Nitrogen / Iron chlorosis) or waterlogging
classes.organic_treatment: Apply decomposed cow dung manure / compost slurry and liquid bio-fertilizer (Azospirillum).
classes.chemical_treatment: Top-dressing of Urea (40-50 kg/ha) or foliar spray of 2% Urea solution.
classes.prevention: Split application of nitrogen at basal, knee-high, and tasseling stages.
classes.weather_action_rule: Heavy rains cause nitrogen leaching; reapply small split dose following heavy downpours.

classes.symptoms: Long, elliptical, grayish-green to tan lesions (cigar-shaped) on leaves, coalescing to cause complete foliage burn.
classes.pathogen: Exserohilum turcicum (Northern Corn Leaf Blight - NCLB)
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar application of Trichoderma viride (10g/L) and copper hydroxide (2g/L).
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5g/L) or Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC (1ml/L).
classes.prevention: Use resistant maize hybrids (Ht gene derivatives), crop rotation, and destruction of infected stubble.
classes.weather_action_rule: High risk during moderate temperatures (18-27°C) with persistent dew or rainy periods.

classes.symptoms: Small, powdery, reddish-brown circular to elongate pustules (uredinia) scattered on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
classes.organic_treatment: Spray sulfur 80% WDG (3g/L) or biocontrol agent Bacillus subtilis.
classes.chemical_treatment: Spray Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (1ml/L) or Azoxystrobin (1ml/L) at first sign of pustules.
classes.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids; plant early in the season to escape peak spore dispersal.
classes.weather_action_rule: Cool, humid weather (16-25°C, >95% RH) strongly favors rust infection.

classes.symptoms: Small, circular brown spots with concentric rings on older lower leaves, developing yellow chlorotic halos.
classes.organic_treatment: Spray copper oxychloride (2.5g/L) or neem seed kernel extract (5%). Prune lower infected leaves up to 30cm off the ground.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray of Chlorothalonil 75% WP (2g/L) or Difenoconazole 25% EC (0.5ml/L).
classes.prevention: Stake plants, mulch soil surface with straw/plastic, avoid overhead irrigation, 3-year crop rotation.
classes.weather_action_rule: High humidity (>80%) and warm temperatures (24-29°C) accelerate disease progression.

classes.symptoms: Rapid daytime wilting and green drooping of the entire plant without prior yellowing; vascular browning visible on stem cut.
classes.organic_treatment: Soil drenching with Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L). Incorporate biochar and mustard cake into soil.
classes.chemical_treatment: Drenching with Streptocycline (100 ppm) + Copper Oxychloride (0.2%).
classes.prevention: Use grafted seedlings on resistant rootstocks, practice solarization of nursery beds, maintain acidic/neutral balance.
classes.weather_action_rule: Warm wet soils (>30°C) with waterlogging create explosive wilt conditions; ensure prompt drainage.

classes.symptoms: Large, irregular, water-soaked, dark brownish-black lesions on leaves and stems with white fungal mold underneath in wet weather.
classes.organic_treatment: Spray Bordeaux mixture (1%) or Copper Hydroxide (2g/L). Remove and destroy all blighted vines.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (2g/L) or Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb (2.5g/L).
classes.prevention: Strictly avoid overhead irrigation; maintain 60cm plant spacing for ventilation; destroy infected plant debris.
classes.weather_action_rule: 🚨 Critical alert: Cool wet weather (15-20°C, >90% RH) can destroy entire crop within 7-10 days. Spray preventive fungicide immediately before expected rainfall.

classes.symptoms: Lush green foliage, uniform growth, abundant flowering and firm blemish-free fruit clusters.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply Panchagavya (3%) or Seaweed extract spray every 2 weeks.
classes.chemical_treatment: Standard fertigation with 19:19:19 and Calcium Nitrate (to prevent blossom end rot).
classes.prevention: Regular trellising, pruning suckers, mulching, and routine biweekly crop scouting.
classes.weather_action_rule: Regulate drip irrigation to maintain 50-60% field capacity moisture.

classes.symptoms: Mottling with alternating light and dark green patches, leaf blistering, 'shoestring' distortion of foliage, and stunting.
classes.pathogen: Tomato mosaic virus (ToMV / TMV) - Mechanically transmitted
classes.organic_treatment: Rogue out infected plants. Dip hands and tools in skim milk or 20% trisodium phosphate during handling.
classes.chemical_treatment: No chemical cure for viral infections. Apply micronutrient and humic acid foliar spray to boost plant vigor.
classes.prevention: Use certified virus-free seeds, avoid smoking/tobacco handling near plants, disinfect trellis wires and stakes.
classes.weather_action_rule: High temperatures (>30°C) intensify mosaic symptom expression.

classes.symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of leaf margins, severe yellow chlorosis of leaf edges, stunted bushy growth, flower abortion.
classes.pathogen: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)
classes.organic_treatment: Install yellow sticky cards (20-25 cards/acre). Spray 5% neem oil emulsion with soap.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray for whitefly vector: Cyantraniliprole 10.26% OD (1.8ml/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (1ml/L).
classes.prevention: Grow seedlings under 40-mesh insect-proof nylon nets, use resistant hybrids (e.g. Ty-1/Ty-3 genes), install reflective silver mulch.
classes.weather_action_rule: Dry, hot weather triggers explosive whitefly proliferation; initiate vector control immediately.

classes.symptoms: Brown, dark circular to angular spots with characteristic concentric target-board rings on older foliage, yellowing surrounding tissue.
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar spray of Copper Hydroxide (2g/L) or neem-based biopesticide (5ml/L). Remove diseased lower canopy leaves.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5g/L) or Chlorothalonil 75% WP (2g/L) or Azoxystrobin (1ml/L).
classes.prevention: Practice 3-year solanaceous crop rotation, certified disease-free seed tubers, avoid sprinkler irrigation.
classes.weather_action_rule: Warm temperatures (24-29°C) with alternating dry and wet periods trigger rapid spore release.

classes.symptoms: Water-soaked irregular dark green to purplish-black lesions starting at leaf tips and margins, white cottony mold on underside in humid conditions.
classes.organic_treatment: Bordeaux mixture (1%) or Copper Oxychloride (2.5g/L). Destroy infected haulms 10 days before harvest.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (2g/L) or Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb (2.5g/L) or Dimethomorph 50% WP (1g/L).
classes.prevention: Hill up soil around tubers (prevent wash-down of zoospores), use resistant cultivars (Kufri Jyoti, Kufri Girdhari).
classes.weather_action_rule: 🚨 High risk: Cool wet weather (12-22°C, RH >90%). Apply protective fungicide immediately before rain.

classes.symptoms: Lush, dark green compound leaves with upright stems and vigorous canopy development without lesions or mottling.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply balanced compost, vermicompost, and biofertilizers (Azotobacter & PSB).
classes.chemical_treatment: Maintain scheduled NPK (120:80:100 kg/ha) fertilization.
classes.prevention: Regular field monitoring, earthing up, weed control, and preventive Trichoderma application.
classes.weather_action_rule: Maintain uniform soil moisture at 65-75% field capacity during tuber bulking.

classes.symptoms: Dull olive-green velvety spots on leaves and fruit, turning dark brown to black and corky with age.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply lime sulfur (2.5ml/L) or wettable sulfur (3g/L) at green tip stage. Prune canopies to improve air circulation.
classes.chemical_treatment: Spray Difenoconazole 25% EC (0.5ml/L) or Captan 50% WP (2g/L) or Dodine 65% WP (1g/L).
classes.prevention: Rake and burn fallen autumn leaves (destroys overwintering pseudothecia); plant scab-resistant rootstocks.
classes.weather_action_rule: Mills period: Spore infection requires leaf wetness of 9+ hours at 15-24°C.

classes.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange circular lesions on upper leaf surfaces with small black dots (pycnia), tube-like aecia on leaf underside.
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar spray of liquid copper or sulfur (3g/L). Remove nearby Eastern red cedar/juniper alternate hosts within 500m.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Myclobutanil 10% WP (1g/L) or Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5g/L) during pink-bud through petal fall.
classes.prevention: Eradicate wild juniper trees near apple orchards; prune out galls from nearby ornamental cedars.
classes.weather_action_rule: Warm spring rains (13-24°C) trigger gelatinous orange spore horns on cedar galls.

classes.symptoms: Frog-eye leaf spots (purple margins with tan centers), black mummified rotting fruit, and sunken stem cankers.
classes.organic_treatment: Prune dead wood and remove mummified apples from orchard floor.
classes.chemical_treatment: Spray Captan 50% WP (2.5g/L) or Thiophanate-methyl 70% WP (1g/L).
classes.prevention: Prune out dead fire-blighted twigs and cankers during winter dormancy.
classes.weather_action_rule: Infection peaks during warm humid rainy spells (20-28°C).

classes.symptoms: Vibrant, dark green serrated leaves and firm developing fruit without lesions, mildew, or distortion.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply organic mulch and foliar seaweed extract for vigor.
classes.chemical_treatment: Maintain standard micronutrient foliar schedule (Boron, Zinc, Calcium).
classes.prevention: Regular orchard scouting, pruning for sunlight penetration, integrated pest management.
classes.weather_action_rule: Maintain adequate irrigation during fruit sizing.

classes.symptoms: Small, water-soaked circular to irregular dark brown lesions on leaves and fruit, causing severe defoliation and fruit drop.
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar spray of Copper Hydroxide (2g/L) combined with Bacillus amyloliquefaciens biocontrol.
classes.chemical_treatment: Spray Copper Oxychloride (2.5g/L) mixed with Streptocycline (100 ppm) at 10-day intervals.
classes.prevention: Use hot-water-treated certified seeds, avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation, rotate with non-solanaceous crops.
classes.weather_action_rule: Rainstorms with wind (>15 km/h) and warm temperatures (24-30°C) cause severe bacterial splash spread.

classes.symptoms: Dark green, smooth, glossy foliage with strong branch development and healthy flower set.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply balanced vermicompost and neem cake at 45-day intervals.
classes.chemical_treatment: Apply balanced NPK (100:60:60 kg/ha) with calcium nitrate side-dressing.
classes.prevention: Scout weekly for thrips and aphids vectors; maintain raised beds for drainage.
classes.weather_action_rule: Maintain drip irrigation at 70% soil water capacity.

classes.symptoms: Yellowing and downward curling of leaf margins (hopper burn), stunted growth, leaves turning bronzed/yellowish with sticky honeydew from jassids, aphids, thrips, and whiteflies.
classes.pathogen: Sucking Pest Complex: Amrasca biguttula (Jassids), Aphis gossypii (Aphids), Bemisia tabaci (Whiteflies), Thrips tabaci
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar spray of 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Neem Oil 1500 ppm @ 3ml/L. Install yellow and blue sticky traps (10-15 traps/acre). Conserve predatory ladybird beetles and chrysoperla.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5ml/L, Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.2g/L, Flonicamid 50% WG @ 0.4g/L, or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.2g/L in 150-200 L water/acre.
classes.prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer which attracts sucking pests. Maintain 90x60 cm plant spacing. Plant castor or maize as trap border crops around cotton field.
classes.weather_action_rule: Dry, warm weather (>30°C) with low relative humidity accelerates sucking pest multiplication. Scout under leaf surfaces every 3-4 days.

classes.symptoms: Upward or downward leaf curling, thickening of leaf veins, enation (leaf-like outgrowths) on lower leaf surface, severe stunting and reduced boll formation.
classes.pathogen: Cotton leaf curl virus (CLCuV - Begomovirus) transmitted by Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)
classes.organic_treatment: Install yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre) at canopy height to trap whitefly vectors. Spray Neem oil (5ml/L) or botanical extracts weekly.
classes.chemical_treatment: Control whitefly vector promptly with Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1ml/L, Pyriproxyfen 10% EC @ 2ml/L, or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.2g/L.
classes.prevention: Eradicate alternate weed hosts (Abutilon indicum, Parthenium) from field borders. Rogue out and burn infected plants before square formation. Plant CLCuV-tolerant hybrids.
classes.weather_action_rule: Hot dry spells trigger whitefly outbreaks. Spray in early morning or late evening targeting leaf undersides.

classes.symptoms: Rosetted flowers ('rose-shaped' locked blooms), bore holes in developing green bolls plugged with excreta, damaged seeds, and stained lint inside mature bolls.
classes.organic_treatment: Install Pheromone Traps with Gossyplure @ 5 traps/acre for monitoring and 10 traps/acre for mass trapping. Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma bactrae @ 60,000/acre at weekly intervals.
classes.chemical_treatment: When ETL is breached (>8 moths/trap/night for 3 consecutive days), spray Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4g/L, Profenofos 50% EC @ 2ml/L, Spinosad 45% SC @ 0.3ml/L, or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3ml/L.
classes.prevention: Avoid extended ratoon cotton crops. Destroy crop residues and shred cotton stalks immediately after final picking. Practice clean cultivation.
classes.weather_action_rule: Moth activity peaks at dusk with warm night temperatures (22-28°C). Time foliar applications in late afternoon for maximum contact efficacy.

classes.symptoms: Angular water-soaked dark brown spots on leaves bounded by veins, black lesion streaks along stems and branches ('black arm'), and water-soaked round spots on bolls.
classes.organic_treatment: Treat seeds with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/kg seed. Spray copper hydroxide (2g/L) during early vegetative growth.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray of Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (2.5g/L) tank-mixed with Streptocycline (1g in 10L water / 100 ppm). Repeat after 12-15 days if conditions persist.
classes.prevention: Acid delinting of cotton seeds with concentrated sulfuric acid (100ml/kg fuzzy seed). Destroy infected crop residues after harvest.
classes.weather_action_rule: Warm rainy weather with wind (25-30°C and >80% RH) spreads bacterial splash. Spray immediately after rainfall subsides.

classes.symptoms: Dark green palmate leaves, vigorous sympodial branching, healthy flower squares and uniform boll retention with zero insect puncture.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply 10 tonnes FYM/acre along with bio-fertilizers (Azotobacter and PSB @ 2kg/acre each).
classes.chemical_treatment: Follow balanced NPK schedule (120:60:60 kg/ha). Apply 2% DAP or 1% 19:19:19 foliar spray during flowering and boll development stages for higher boll retention.
classes.prevention: Regular field scouting for sucking pests and bollworms. Maintain furrow irrigation intervals (every 10-15 days in black soil).
classes.weather_action_rule: Irrigate at critical growth phases: square formation, peak flowering, and boll development.

classes.symptoms: Discoloration and drying of the 3rd and 4th upper leaves from tip down, internal cane stalk turning reddish with distinctive white transverse cross-patches and alcoholic fermented smell.
classes.organic_treatment: Treat seed setts with Trichoderma viride / harzianum (10g/L) for 20 mins. Enrich planting furrow with 2.5 tonnes FYM mixed with 5kg Trichoderma.
classes.chemical_treatment: Sett dipping in Carbendazim 50% WP (1g/L) or Thiophanate Methyl 70% WP (1g/L) for 15 minutes before planting. Drench infected stool spots with Copper Oxychloride (3g/L).
classes.prevention: Use certified disease-free nursery seed cane (heat-treated setts). Rogue out infected clumps and burn them. Practice 2-year crop rotation with rice or green manure.
classes.weather_action_rule: High humidity (85-90%) and waterlogging during monsoon trigger epidemic spread. Ensure furrow surface drainage.

classes.symptoms: Production of a long, black, whip-like unbranched curved structure from the apical terminal shoot, covered with silvery membrane containing millions of black teliospores.
classes.organic_treatment: Carefully cover the smut whip with a polythene bag before cutting at base, then immerse in boiling water or burn to prevent airborne spore dissemination.
classes.chemical_treatment: Sett treatment with Triadimefon 25% WP @ 1g/L or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1g/L for 15 minutes before planting.
classes.prevention: Plant smut-resistant sugarcane varieties (e.g., Co 86032, Co 0238). Avoid ratooning of heavily diseased cane fields.
classes.weather_action_rule: Dry, windy weather facilitates spore dispersal. Prune whips early in the morning when dew keeps spores moist.

classes.symptoms: Leaves turning yellowish-white with pale blotches, covered with dense black sooty mold fungus feeding on sugary excretions of pyrilla leafhoppers and aphids.
classes.organic_treatment: Conserve the natural nymphal and adult ecto-parasitoid Epiricania melanoleuca (release 4000-5000 cocoons/acre). Spray 5% Neem extract.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 2ml/L or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3ml/L targeting the lower leaf canopy where leafhoppers congregate.
classes.prevention: Detrash lower dry leaves at 120 and 150 days after planting to reduce egg masses and improve air circulation.
classes.weather_action_rule: Warm, humid conditions following intermittent monsoon showers favor rapid Pyrilla multiplication.

classes.symptoms: Thick solid canes, dark green broad erect leaves, healthy root crown, and high brix sugar accumulation.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply press mud (10 tonnes/ha) or vermicompost + Gluconacetobacter diazotrophicus (nitrogen-fixing endophyte @ 5kg/ha).
classes.chemical_treatment: Apply recommended NPK (250:100:120 kg/ha). Apply Nitrogen in 3 splits (sowing, 45 DAP, and earthing up at 90 DAP).
classes.prevention: Trash mulching in alternate furrows to conserve soil moisture, reduce weed pressure, and improve soil organic carbon.
classes.weather_action_rule: Irrigate at 7-10 day intervals during summer formative phase (45-100 days after planting).

classes.symptoms: Spindle-shaped elliptical lesions on leaves with brown/reddish-brown borders and whitish-grey centers ('leaf blast'); blackened rotting neck node causing lodging and empty white heads ('neck blast').
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar spray with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 2.5g/L or Trichoderma viride @ 5g/L. Treat seeds with bio-agent (10g/kg seed).
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L, Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5ml/L, or Kasugamycin 3% SL @ 2ml/L at early lesion appearance.
classes.prevention: Avoid excessive split applications of Nitrogen fertilizer. Maintain 2-3 cm standing water in paddy fields. Plant blast-resistant varieties (e.g., Swarna-Sub1, MTU 1010).
classes.weather_action_rule: Cool night temperatures (18-22°C), high relative humidity (>90%), and prolonged dew periods favor blast outbreaks. Spray immediately at boot leaf stage.

classes.symptoms: Water-soaked yellowish-green stripes initiating from leaf tips/margins, developing wavy undulating edges, turning bleached straw-yellow with milky bacterial ooze droplets in early morning.
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar spray of fresh cow dung slurry extract (20g/L filtered) or neem oil (3ml/L). Treat seeds with hot water (52-54°C for 10 min).
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (2.5g/L) mixed with Streptocycline (1g in 10L water / 100 ppm) or Plantomycin (1g/L).
classes.prevention: Drain excess water from nursery/field during disease outbreak. Delay top-dressing of nitrogen until disease spread ceases. Practice balanced potash application (K₂O @ 50kg/ha).
classes.weather_action_rule: Monsoon cyclones, stormy winds, and flooding create micro-injuries in rice leaves allowing rapid bacterial entry.

classes.symptoms: Oval or oblong greenish-grey water-soaked spots with dark brown margins on leaf sheaths just above water level, expanding into irregular blotches covering whole sheath and leaf blades.
classes.organic_treatment: Soil application of Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 2.5 kg/ha mixed with 50 kg well-decomposed FYM at planting.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 2ml/L, Validamycin 3% L @ 2.5ml/L, or Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1ml/L at tiller stage.
classes.prevention: Maintain optimal seedling spacing (20x15 cm) to avoid excessively dense canopy humidity. Clean bunds and eliminate grassy weeds.
classes.weather_action_rule: High relative humidity (85-100%) and warm temperatures (28-32°C) inside dense canopy trigger sclerotial germination.

classes.symptoms: Numerous small circular to oval dark brown spots (0.5 to 2 cm) distributed uniformly on leaves and glumes, often with yellow halo around lesions.
classes.organic_treatment: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4g/kg seed. Apply organic manure to correct soil nutrient deficiency.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L or Edifenphos 50% EC @ 1ml/L.
classes.prevention: Correct soil nutrient imbalances (especially Nitrogen, Potassium, and Silicon deficiency). Avoid water stress in dry direct-seeded rice.
classes.weather_action_rule: Cloudy weather with high humidity (80-90%) and rain showers promote rapid conidial sporulation.

classes.symptoms: Robust green tillers, clean sheaths and leaf blades without lesions, healthy golden-yellow panicles with 100% grain filling.
classes.organic_treatment: Incorporate green manure (Dhaincha/Sesbania) @ 20-25 kg seed/ha before transplanting. Apply Azospirillum @ 2 kg/ha.
classes.chemical_treatment: Apply NPK (100:50:50 kg/ha). Apply Zinc Sulfate @ 25 kg/ha as basal dose to prevent Khaira disease (zinc deficiency).
classes.prevention: Practice alternate wetting and drying (AWD) irrigation to improve root aeration and reduce methane emissions by 30%.
classes.weather_action_rule: Maintain 5 cm shallow standing water during critical panicle initiation and flowering stages.

classes.disease_name: Wheat Yellow Rust and Stripe Rust
classes.symptoms: Bright yellow, small spherical pustules arranged in characteristic continuous linear stripes on the leaf blades, turning chlorotic and necrotic.
classes.pathogen: Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Fungal Pathogen)
classes.organic_treatment: Spray wettable sulfur (3g/L). Plant certified stripe-rust resistant wheat varieties (e.g., HD 2967, DBW 187, DBW 222).
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt) @ 1ml/L or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1ml/L in 200 L water/acre as soon as yellow rust foci are scouted.
classes.prevention: Conduct regular surveillance in sub-mountainous and northern wheat belts from December to February. Eliminate volunteer host grasses.
classes.weather_action_rule: Cool temperatures (10-15°C) and high humidity/morning dew create ideal conditions for stripe rust development.

classes.disease_name: Wheat Brown Rust and Leaf Rust
classes.symptoms: Small, round to oval orange-brown powdery pustules scattered randomly (not in stripes) across the upper surface of leaves, causing premature senescence.
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar application of bio-agent Trichoderma viride @ 5g/L. Seed dressing with Trichoderma @ 4g/kg seed.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L.
classes.prevention: Avoid late sowing; plant recommended high-yielding rust-resistant varieties before November 15-25.
classes.weather_action_rule: Moderate temperatures (18-25°C) in late winter/spring trigger leaf rust escalation.

classes.symptoms: Only a few grains per ear head converted into black powdery teliospore masses, emitting a foul, rotting-fish odor (caused by trimethylamine).
classes.organic_treatment: Use certified bunt-free seeds. Treat seed with Trichoderma viride @ 4g/kg.
classes.chemical_treatment: Seed treatment with Carboxin 37.5% + Thiram 37.5% DS @ 2g/kg seed. Foliar spray of Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L at ear emergence (heading) stage.
classes.prevention: Avoid excessive irrigation during wheat ear-heading and flowering stages. Practice crop rotation with non-cereal crops.
classes.weather_action_rule: Light rain or high humidity during wheat flowering period (February) facilitates airborne sporidial infection.

classes.symptoms: Erect lush green tillers, strong straw resisting lodging, fully filled compact ear heads with bold golden grains.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply 10 tonnes FYM/ha + Azotobacter bio-fertilizer seed inoculation.
classes.chemical_treatment: Apply NPK (120:60:40 kg/ha). Apply Nitrogen in 3 splits: 1/2 basal, 1/4 at CRI stage (21 DAS), and 1/4 at late jointing stage.
classes.prevention: Schedule critical irrigations at: 1. Crown Root Initiation (CRI - 21 DAS), 2. Tillering (40-45 DAS), 3. Late Jointing (60-65 DAS), 4. Flowering (80-85 DAS), and 5. Milk stage (100-105 DAS).
classes.weather_action_rule: Avoid irrigation during strong windy spells (>15 km/h) at maturity stage to prevent crop lodging.

classes.symptoms: Clear yellow network of veins against green lamina on leaves, complete chlorosis/yellowing of younger foliage, dwarfed plants, and hard, yellow, deformed unmarketable fruits.
classes.pathogen: Okra yellow vein mosaic virus (OYVMV - Begomovirus) transmitted by Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)
classes.organic_treatment: Install yellow sticky traps (15 traps/acre). Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Neem Oil 1500 ppm @ 3ml/L every 10 days.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5ml/L, Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.3g/L, or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3g/L to control vector.
classes.prevention: Rogue out infected plants early. Plant YVMV-resistant okra hybrids (e.g., Arka Anamika, Parbhani Kranti, Kashi Kranti).
classes.weather_action_rule: High temperature (>32°C) combined with dry air triggers rapid whitefly breeding. Scout leaf undersides weekly.

classes.symptoms: Wilting and drooping of tender terminal growing shoots; bore holes in developing pods plugged with larval frass/excreta; twisted, distorted fruits.
classes.pathogen: Earias vittella and Earias insulana (Spotted Bollworm / Fruit Borer)
classes.organic_treatment: Install Pheromone traps @ 5/acre for monitoring. Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis @ 50,000/acre. Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) @ 2g/L.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4g/L, Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3ml/L, or Spinosad 45% SC @ 0.3ml/L in 150 L water/acre.
classes.prevention: Clip and destroy infested shoots along with larvae during early crop stage. Collect and safely dispose of all bored fruits.
classes.weather_action_rule: Warm humid weather accelerates borer generations. Spray in late evening when borer larvae become active.

classes.symptoms: Broad, vibrant dark green leaves, vigorous flowering, straight tender green fruits with crisp texture.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply 10 tonnes FYM/acre + 2.5 tonnes vermicompost. Apply Panchagavya 3% as foliar spray at 30 and 45 DAS.
classes.chemical_treatment: Apply NPK (100:50:50 kg/ha). Apply Nitrogen in 3 splits (basal, 30 days, and 60 days). Spray 19:19:19 (5g/L) during peak fruiting.
classes.prevention: Harvest fruits every 2-3 days to maintain continuous flowering and pod set. Maintain furrow irrigation at 4-6 day intervals in summer.
classes.weather_action_rule: Maintain soil moisture without water stagnation; okra is sensitive to root waterlogging.

classes.symptoms: Small, circular reddish-brown spots with dark borders on leaves with tiny black pycnidia; shriveled, hard, wrinkled bluish-black mummified berries hanging on clusters.
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar spray with Bordeaux mixture (1%) or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (2.5g/L). Prune out and bury all mummified grape clusters.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L, Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1g/L, or Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1ml/L starting from new shoot growth through 4 weeks post-bloom.
classes.prevention: Open vine canopy via shoot positioning and leaf removal around fruit clusters to maximize air movement and sunlight.
classes.weather_action_rule: Rainy periods with warm temperatures (21-32°C) trigger ascospore discharge and rapid fruit infection.

classes.symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis and necrotic patches creating a striking 'tiger-stripe' pattern on leaves; dark purple/black speckling and cracked skin on berries ('measles').
classes.pathogen: Fomitiporia mediterranea, Phaeomoniella chlamydospora, Phaeoacremonium minimum complex
classes.organic_treatment: Apply Trichoderma-based pruning wound sealants (10% paste) immediately to fresh cuts after winter pruning.
classes.chemical_treatment: Disinfect pruning shears with 70% alcohol. Treat pruning cuts with Copper Hydroxide or Thiophanate-methyl wound paste.
classes.prevention: Avoid pruning during wet, rainy days when airborne fungal spores are abundant. Rogue severely infected declining grapevines.
classes.weather_action_rule: Prune during dry winter periods. Hot summer weather induces sudden vine collapse (apoplexy).

classes.symptoms: Lush green palmate foliage, clean cane framework, robust uniform berry clusters with natural bloom powder and high Brix sugar content.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply 15 tonnes FYM/acre after pruning + bio-fertilizers (VAM + PSB @ 5kg/acre each).
classes.chemical_treatment: Follow balanced fertigation: N-P-K (150:100:200 kg/ha) with regular Calcium and Potassium during berry enlargement stage.
classes.prevention: Systematic canopy management: shoot thinning, bunch thinning, and berry sizing gibberellic acid (GA3) protocols.
classes.weather_action_rule: Drip irrigation scheduled based on FAO-56 pan evaporation model (6-8 mm/day in peak fruit growth).

classes.symptoms: White or creamy-yellow raised blister-like pustules on lower leaf surface; hypertrophied, swollen, and distorted floral parts forming 'staghead' malformations.
classes.organic_treatment: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4g/kg seed. Prune and destroy staghead floral malformations early.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Ridomil Gold) @ 2g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L at 45-50 and 60-65 DAS.
classes.prevention: Sow mustard early (first fortnight of October) to escape peak white rust incidence. Plant resistant varieties (e.g., NRCHB 101, DRMRIJ 31).
classes.weather_action_rule: Cool moist weather (12-18°C) with morning fog and high relative humidity (>85%) facilitates oospore germination.

classes.symptoms: Masses of small green-to-black sucking insects clustering on tender shoots, inflorescences, and pods, causing leaf curling, stunted growth, and poor seed filling.
classes.organic_treatment: Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Neem oil 1500 ppm @ 3ml/L. Conserve Coccinellid predator beetles (ladybirds).
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Dimethoate 30% EC @ 1.7ml/L, Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3ml/L, or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3g/L when aphid population exceeds ETL (1.5-2 cm colony on shoot).
classes.prevention: Practice timely sowing before October 20. Apply balanced nitrogen; avoid excess urea which makes foliage succulent and prone to aphids.
classes.weather_action_rule: Cloudy, calm weather with temperatures between 15-20°C triggers rapid aphid population surges.

classes.symptoms: Strong primary and secondary branching, vibrant golden-yellow flowering, and densely packed healthy green siliquae (pods).
classes.organic_treatment: Apply 8-10 tonnes FYM/ha + Azotobacter bio-fertilizer.
classes.chemical_treatment: Apply NPK (80:40:40 kg/ha) with essential Sulfur @ 40 kg/ha (elemental sulfur or gypsum) to boost seed oil content by 2-3%.
classes.prevention: Provide two critical irrigations: 1st at flowering stage (30-35 DAS) and 2nd at pod development stage (60-65 DAS).
classes.weather_action_rule: Ensure honeybee hive presence (2-3 boxes/acre) for high cross-pollination and 25% yield boost.

classes.symptoms: Early leaf spots (Cercospora arachidicola): circular reddish-brown spots with prominent bright yellow halo. Late leaf spots (Phaeoisariopsis personata): small circular dark black spots without halo on lower leaf surface.
classes.pathogen: Cercospora arachidicola and Phaeoisariopsis personata (Fungal Complex)
classes.organic_treatment: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4g/kg seed. Foliar spray of 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) at 40 and 60 DAS.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 2ml/L, Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L + Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1g/L, or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1ml/L.
classes.prevention: Crop rotation with cereal crops (Maize, Sorghum, Pearl Millet). Burn infected crop haulms after harvest.
classes.weather_action_rule: High relative humidity (>80%) and temperatures between 25-30°C for 3 consecutive days favor severe defoliation.

classes.symptoms: Dense dark green 4-foliolate canopy, vigorous peg penetration into soil, and well-developed double-seeded pods with clean shells.
classes.organic_treatment: Seed inoculation with Rhizobium leguminosarum + PSB @ 250g/10kg seeds. Apply 10 tonnes FYM/ha.
classes.chemical_treatment: Apply NPK (25:50:50 kg/ha) + Gypsum @ 500 kg/ha in two splits (1/2 at sowing, 1/2 at pegging stage 40-45 DAS) for pod filling and calcium supply.
classes.prevention: Keep soil loose around root zone for easy peg entry; avoid hoeing after peg initiation (45 DAS).
classes.weather_action_rule: Maintain light, frequent irrigations during flowering, pegging, and pod development phases.

classes.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves and seed stalks that rapidly turn purple with dark concentric rings and broad yellow halos, leading to leaf tipping, drying, and stalk breakage.
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar spray of Trichoderma viride @ 5g/L with a sticking agent (surfactant). Crop rotation with pulses or maize.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L or Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1ml/L with 0.5ml/L wetting agent / sticker (Sandovit/Triton).
classes.prevention: Ensure good drainage; plant on raised beds (15 cm high). Maintain 15x10 cm spacing. Avoid excessive overhead sprinkler irrigation.
classes.weather_action_rule: Warm humid conditions (25-30°C and 80-90% RH) following rain trigger rapid lesion enlargement.

classes.symptoms: Minute yellowish-brown insects causing silvery-white blotches, patches, and curled leaf tips due to rasping and sucking sap from leaf sheaths.
classes.organic_treatment: Install blue and yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre). Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Beauveria bassiana @ 5g/L.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Fipronil 5% SC @ 1.5ml/L, Profenofos 50% EC @ 2ml/L, or Spinosad 45% SC @ 0.3ml/L targeting the inner leaf axils with sticking agent.
classes.prevention: Clean field bunds of alternative hosts. Provide barrier crops like two rows of maize around the onion plot.
classes.weather_action_rule: Hot, dry weather favors massive thrips population spikes. Overhead irrigation helps wash thrips off foliage.

classes.symptoms: Erect, hollow cylindrical dark green leaves with heavy waxy bloom, thick necks transitioning cleanly into solid tight bulbs.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply 15 tonnes FYM/acre + Azospirillum @ 2 kg/ha.
classes.chemical_treatment: Apply NPK (100:50:50 kg/ha) + Sulfur @ 30 kg/ha. Apply Nitrogen in splits: 1/2 basal, 1/4 at 30 DAT, and 1/4 at 45 DAT. Withhold Nitrogen after 60 DAT to avoid thick necks.
classes.prevention: Stop irrigation 10-15 days prior to harvest for field curing and maximum bulb storage shelf-life.
classes.weather_action_rule: Ensure uniform soil moisture during bulb enlargement phase.

classes.symptoms: Drooping and wilting of growing shoot tips in young plants; bore holes on fruits plugged with caterpillar excreta (frass), rendering fruits rotten and unmarketable.
classes.organic_treatment: Install Pheromone traps with Lucinlure @ 12 traps/acre. Clip and destroy infested shoots weekly. Spray Bacillus thuringiensis @ 2g/L.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4g/L, Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3ml/L, or Flubendiamide 39.35% SC @ 0.3ml/L in 150 L water/acre.
classes.prevention: Continuous prompt destruction of infested shoots and bored fruits. Avoid continuous solanaceous cropping in the same plot.
classes.weather_action_rule: Moths are active during warm humid nights. Time foliar sprays in late afternoon hours.

classes.symptoms: Extremely small, soft yellow leaves clustered densely like a rosette, phylloid green floral structures, and complete bushy stunting with zero fruit set.
classes.pathogen: Phytoplasma transmitted by leafhopper vector (Hishimonus phycitis)
classes.organic_treatment: Immediately rogue out and bury infected plants to remove pathogen reservoir. Spray neem oil (3ml/L) to suppress leafhopper vectors.
classes.chemical_treatment: Spray systemic insecticide Dimethoate 30% EC @ 1.5ml/L or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.4ml/L to control leafhopper vectors in the nursery and main field.
classes.prevention: Treat nursery beds with Phorate 10G or Carbofuran. Plant resistant brinjal cultivars.
classes.weather_action_rule: High leafhopper populations occur during warm post-monsoon months.

classes.symptoms: Sturdy erect plants, broad velvety deep green leaves, vibrant purple flowers, and smooth glossy fruits.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply 10 tonnes FYM/acre + 2.5 tonnes vermicompost. Apply Panchagavya 3% as foliar tonic every 20 days.
classes.chemical_treatment: Apply NPK (100:50:50 kg/ha). Apply Potassium (K₂O) for shiny fruit skin and disease resistance.
classes.prevention: Maintain 75x60 cm plant spacing. Harvest mature glossy fruits regularly every 4-5 days.
classes.weather_action_rule: Irrigate at 4-6 day intervals in summer and 8-10 day intervals in winter.

classes.symptoms: Tiny, brown to reddish-brown raised pustules on lower surface of leaves, progressing rapidly to yellowing and premature leaf defoliation during pod filling.
classes.organic_treatment: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 5g/kg seed. Spray 5% neem extract at early vegetative stage.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 2ml/L, Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L, or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1ml/L at first appearance of pustules.
classes.prevention: Plant rust-tolerant varieties (e.g., JS 335, NRC 37, MACS 450). Avoid late sowing.
classes.weather_action_rule: Extended leaf wetness (>6 hours), high humidity (>80%), and temperatures between 18-26°C trigger explosive rust spread.

classes.symptoms: Lush green trifoliate canopy, strong root nodulation, vigorous flowering racemes, and well-filled 3-seeded pods.
classes.organic_treatment: Seed treatment with Bradyrhizobium japonicum + PSB @ 500g/ha seed.
classes.chemical_treatment: Apply NPK (30:60:40 kg/ha) + Sulfur @ 20 kg/ha (as Gypsum) to enhance seed protein and oil content.
classes.prevention: Ensure good field drainage to avoid root waterlogging during heavy monsoon downpours.
classes.weather_action_rule: Provide supplemental irrigation during pod development phase if monsoon breaks for >10 days.

classes.symptoms: Asymmetrical blotchy mottled chlorosis/yellowing on leaves, small upright chlorotic leaves (zinc-deficiency like), lopsided sour green fruits with aborted seeds.
classes.pathogen: Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (Bacterial Pathogen transmitted by Asian Citrus Psyllid - Diaphorina citri)
classes.organic_treatment: Install yellow sticky traps (15/acre). Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE). Rogue and burn severely declining trees.
classes.chemical_treatment: Control psyllid vectors with Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5ml/L, Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3g/L, or Dimethoate 30% EC @ 1.5ml/L. Apply foliar micronutrient blend (Zinc 0.5% + Ferrous 0.5% + Manganese 0.5% + Boron 0.1%).
classes.prevention: Plant certified disease-free budwood stock from registered nurseries. Eliminate Murraya paniculata (Kamini - alternate host) from orchard vicinity.
classes.weather_action_rule: Flush shoots during spring and post-monsoon attract dense psyllid vector populations. Target foliar sprays on new flushes.

classes.symptoms: Raised, corky, rough brownish crater-like blister lesions with characteristic water-soaked oily yellow halos on leaves, twigs, thorns, and fruit rinds.
classes.organic_treatment: Prune cankered twigs before monsoon flush and burn them. Spray Bordeaux mixture (1%) before new flushes emerge.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5g/L mixed with Streptocycline @ 1g in 10L water (100 ppm). Repeat 2-3 times during rainy season.
classes.prevention: Control citrus leaf miner (Phyllocnistis citrella) using Spinosad 45% SC @ 0.3ml/L; leaf miner larval galleries serve as primary bacterial entry portals.
classes.weather_action_rule: Wind-driven rains and overhead irrigation disperse bacterial inoculum across orchard trees.

classes.symptoms: Deep glossy dark green foliage, well-spaced canopy framework, abundant fragrant blossom set, and uniform spherical golden-orange fruits.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply 25-30 kg well-rotted FYM + 2 kg neem cake per mature tree annually.
classes.chemical_treatment: Apply balanced NPK per mature tree (600g N, 200g P₂O₅, 400g K₂O) in split doses with annual micronutrient foliar sprays.
classes.prevention: Maintain clean ring basin irrigation; keep tree trunk dry to prevent Phytophthora gummosis / foot rot.
classes.weather_action_rule: Withhold irrigation for 3-4 weeks (bahar treatment) followed by light irrigation to stimulate uniform flowering.

classes.symptoms: Talcum-powder-like white talc patches on upper and lower surfaces of leaves and stems, leaves turning chlorotic, brown, and brittle, with premature leaf drop.
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar spray of Wettable Sulfur 80% WP (3g/L), Potassium Bicarbonate (3g/L), or diluted milk-water solution (1:9 ratio).
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 1ml/L, Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5ml/L, or Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1ml/L.
classes.prevention: Plant resistant cucurbit varieties. Ensure wide plant spacing (1.5m x 1m) and trellis support for airflow.
classes.weather_action_rule: Dry, warm days (20-28°C) with humid nights promote conidial germination without requiring free surface water.

classes.symptoms: Broad expansive dark green lobed leaves, vibrant yellow blossoms, and firm unblemished green/yellow squash fruits.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply 10 tonnes FYM/acre + vermicompost. Apply bio-stimulant sea-weed extract (2ml/L) during flowering.
classes.chemical_treatment: Apply NPK (80:50:50 kg/ha) with drip fertigation. Supplement Calcium nitrate during fruit development.
classes.prevention: Mulch beds with silver/black plastic mulch to prevent soil-borne fruit rot and suppress weeds.
classes.weather_action_rule: Drip irrigate at root zone early in the morning; keep foliage completely dry.

classes.symptoms: Numerous small, irregular, purplish-to-dark-brown spots that lack a white center, coalescing to cause entire leaf margins to look burnt or scorched.
classes.organic_treatment: Foliar spray with Copper Oxychloride (2g/L). Remove and destroy all old spotted leaves after harvest.
classes.chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Captan 50% WP @ 2.5g/L, Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L, or Pyraclostrobin 20% WG @ 1g/L.
classes.prevention: Plant on raised plastic-mulched beds to elevate fruit and leaves above soil. Avoid overhead sprinkler watering.
classes.weather_action_rule: Frequent spring rains and temperatures between 15-25°C favor conidial release.

classes.symptoms: Trifoliate glossy dark green leaves, bright white flowers with golden centers, and conical vibrant red berries with sweet aroma.
classes.organic_treatment: Apply 15 tonnes FYM/ha + VAM bio-fertilizer before planting runner plugs.
classes.chemical_treatment: Apply fertigation NPK (100:60:120 kg/ha) with special focus on Potassium and Calcium for fruit firmness.
classes.prevention: Maintain drip irrigation under black plastic mulch to eliminate soil splash onto berries.
classes.weather_action_rule: Protect flowering crowns from frost with poly-tunnels or row covers when temperature drops below 2°C.
